newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economic recovery to become firmer -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan economic recovery to become firmer -- EPA.

text.p: Japan's economic recovery may slow down temporarily as a result of the rise in the sales tax, but the slowdown will not undermine the overall recovery trend, which is likely to become firmer, a senior official of the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said on Friday.

"There may be a slowdown, but it (the recovery) will not stop and will start moving again. The economic recovery will likely become firmer," Akira Furukawa, director of the EPA's national economic division research bureau, told Reuters Financial Television.
Although the agency needed to keep close watch on the impact of the tax increase on demand, the current economic environment was not all that pessimistic, Furukawa said.

He said the environment for households was not so bad given improvements in employment conditions and steady wages. The economy as a whole was also entering into a favourable economic cycle, Furukawa said.
Asked about the 1.9 percent rise in domestic wholesale prices in April, Furukawa said that the rise simply reflected the increase in the consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1.

Prices are being pushed up because of the rise in import-related goods stemming from the weaker yen and higher oil prices, but this factor was also being offset by rising competition among manufacturers, he said.
"I expect prices to be stable with the pause in the weakening of the yen and competition both at home and abroad," Furukawa said.

Furukawa said he said he did not think the rise in long-term prime rates would directly affect corporate capital investment. The increase in such investment had been supported by good company profits and an increase in demand, he said.
"But we must keep watch since good profits were supported by low interest rates."
